newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's KLSE to start Islamic stock index.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's KLSE to start Islamic stock index.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) will establish an index of stocks which comply with Islamic business practices, the national Bernama news agency reported on Monday.
The agency quoted Malaysia's Deputy Finance Minister Affifudin Omar, who spoke at a conference on Islamic finance on Monday.

"We are looking at about 300 companies whose activities will not be in forbidden activities as stated under Syariah (Islamic) principles like gambling and selling liquor," he told reporters after the speech.
The move is in line with government objectives to create an Islamic banking system which will function along-side the conventional one.

In 1993, the government introduced an 'Interest-free Banking Scheme' which encouraged financial institutions in Malaysia to offer a range of products which complied with the interest-free tenets of Islam.
